description: Hallo! Ich bin Schülerin und interessiere mich für Luft- und Raumfahrt, Ingenieurwesen, Physik, Mathe und Programmieren. Ich suche motivierte Leute, die meinem Team beitreten und gemeinsam an einem Space-Projekt arbeiten! Die Veranstaltung findet in Hamburg statt, und verschiedene Sprachen sind willkommen.
summary:
🚀 Project: Mars Survival

Mars Survival is an interactive web-based project developed using Python and Streamlit. The idea behind this project is to make learning about space science and aerospace engineering more interesting by allowing users to experience some of the real challenges of a Mars mission.

Our project is divided into three stages:

Stage 1 – Gravity Calculation: Players calculate the gravity on Mars using a given scientific formula.

Stage 2 – Asteroid Survival: Players face an asteroid challenge and calculate the fuel required to survive the journey.

Stage 3 – Mars Landing: Players calculate the total amount of fuel needed to land safely on Mars, while considering the possibility of fuel leakage due to damaged fuel lines.

We have included scientific formulas, hints and instant feedback to help players understand the calculations. Each stage unlocks only after successfully completing the previous one.
details:
We built Mars Survival because we wanted to turn the real-life physics of a Mars/Space mission into something anyone can actually play and enjoy. Instead of just reading formulas in a textbook, players step into the shoes of a mission specialist, calibrating Mars's gravity and calculating exact fuel loads with the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation to keep their crew alive.

Our main goal was to make space science feel less intimidating and way more exciting, especially for students or anyone curious about how space travel really works. Under the hood, we coded the whole game in Python using Streamlit for the interface, and used GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud so anyone can open the link and start playing right away in their browser without downloading a thing. When putting it all together, our team focused on striking the right balance between real aerospace math and a smooth, forgiving player experience, adding emergency hints and clear alerts so players learn as they go rather than getting stuck.
